provenance.source_name: Man hammering with a constant beat
provenance.creator: felix.blume
provenance.modifications: HQ ogg preview, then cut to a beat-aligned 3.60s excerpt (source is 118.5s). Onset analysis put the hammering's beat period at ~0.60s; the cut is exactly 6 periods starting 20ms before a strike transient, so the loop wraps onto the next strike instead of drifting. This is the only asset in the ledger cut for LOOP alignment rather than just length - re-cutting it needs the same beat-integer discipline or the loop will audibly stutter at the seam.

assets.integration_note: Sustained loop, NOT an fx one-shot. Declared in LOOP_SFX_NAMES (client/src/audio.js) so its Howl is built with loop:true, and driven by audio.setLoop('repair_start_loop', anyRepairing) once per frame in GameScene's structure loop, where anyRepairing is true if ANY structure's ds.repairMs > 0. State-driven rather than edge-driven: the server zeroes repairMs the tick a channel lapses, so a cancelled/finished repair stops the loop with no stop event.

provenance.creator: iluppai
provenance.modifications: HQ ogg preview, unmodified before the pipeline. Picked a bright SMALL bell deliberately: the obvious feudal-Asian choice was a Kyoto temple bell, but that timbre is already 'death' (fs609028) and a repair finishing must not read like a player dying.

assets.integration_note: One-shot via FX_MAP['repair_done'] (client/src/audio.js). server/game/repair.js's tickRepairChannels pushes {type:'repair_done'} at the structure's footprint centre on the tick a channel completes.

FIELD-WIDE, not per-structure - N firepits sound like one, which is the intended mix.
